claims.source: NASA SP-5110, 55-Nitinol: The Alloy With a Memory, Battelle Memorial Institute for NASA, 1972, chapter 1 p. 1 and references 12 and 74, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720022818/downloads/19720022818.pdf ; NASA CR-1433, Nitinol Characterization Study, September 1969, foreword p. iii and p. 2, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19690026989/downloads/19690026989.pdf ; US Patent 3,174,851, https://patents.google.com/patent/US3174851A/en
claims.text: The federal literature on nitinol, one report of it written by Battelle itself, does not support a Battelle 1948-49 lineage for the alloy. NASA SP-5110, prepared for NASA by Battelle Memorial Institute in 1972, opens: 'Some 10 years ago, Buehler and Wiley of the U.S. Naval Ordnance Laboratory developed a series of engineering alloys that possess a unique mechanical (shape) memory. The generic name of the series of alloys is 55-Nitinol, where Nitinol stands for Nickel Titanium Naval Ordnance Laboratory.' The earliest Naval Ordnance Laboratory nitinol report cited anywhere in its reference list is NOLTR 61-75 of 3 August 1961; US Patent 3,174,851 was filed on 1 December 1961; and NASA CR-1433 of September 1969 records Battelle's own role as a subcontractor to Goodyear Aerospace which 'processed the basic Nitinol rod'. The allegation that Wright-Patterson-sponsored Battelle reports on nickel-titanium alloy from 1948-49 are missing from Air Force and Battelle archives is kept on this board as the allegation it is, and is unsupported by the federal literature opened here.

connections.label: Project Blue Book
connections.note: TIER 3, INFERENTIAL, and the reason is worth stating. Project Blue Book Special Report No. 14, the statistical analysis of 1947-1952 sighting reports dated 5 May 1955, is attributed on its own title page to the Air Technical Intelligence Center at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, under Project No. 10073. Its summary says the study 'was prepared by a panel of scientists both in and out of the Air Force'. The released copy names no contractor at all: a full-text scan of all 313 pages finds no occurrence of 'Battelle', 'Columbus' or 'Memorial Institute'. The Columbus tie rests entirely on the secondary literature's Battelle attribution, which the primary record does not make.

desc: Battelle Memorial Institute has been headquartered in Columbus, Ohio since 1929. The distance from Columbus to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton is roughly sixty-five miles - close enough that Battelle was the natural contractor for Air Force materials and analytical work throughout the 1940s and 1950s, including the nickel-titanium alloy research from which nitinol emerged and the Project Stork analysis of Project Blue Book's case files. Copy No. 35 of Blue Book Special Report No. 14 bears Ohio markings. The geography explains the persistence: the Air Force's technical intelligence centre and the country's largest private applied science institute sat an hour apart, and the analytical work on unidentified objects moved between them for a decade.
